post.caption: Timex lost a watch on live TV. Timex grew out of a Connecticut clock company founded in 1854, and its first wristwatch came out in 1950. Its ads showed watches surviving torture tests, and in 1956 the tests moved to live television with former news anchor John Cameron Swayze. In one live ad he strapped a watch to an outboard motor, lowered it into a tank, and when he tipped the blades up the watch was gone. He said it was probably at the bottom, still ticking. By 1962, about a third of American watch sales were Timex.
